q: 1. In general equation for the deflection of the beam: M=EI*  where EI is
explain: EI represent the flexural strength.

q: 2. A frame is completely analyzed when
options: the variation in shear is found throughout the frame
the variation in direct stress, shear and moment is found throughout the frame
the shear and moment reaction from member to member are known at every joint
explain: A rigid frame analysis is complete only when all three internal force quantities—axial (direct) force, shear force, and bending moment—are known throughout every member.

q: 3. When the load does not pass through the shear centre of the steel beam. It produces
options: torsional moment along with bending moment
explain: Loads not passing through the shear center cause twisting (torsion). The resistance to this is related to the torsional and sectional rigidity of the beam.

q: 4. When a cantilever beam of length l is loaded with a uniformly varying load of maximum intensity w at free end, the shape of bending moment diagram is
explain: Since the load is linear (varying), the shear force is parabolic ($x^2$), and the bending moment is a cubic function ($x^3$).

q: 5. If the span of real beam is l, the span of the corresponding conjugate beam is
explain: In the conjugate beam method, the conjugate beam has the same span (length) as the real beam; only the support conditions and loading (M/EI diagram) change.

q: 6. The loading on the conjugate beam will be
options: loading on the real beam divided by EI
B.M. diagram divided by SF diagram
explain: The conjugate beam method loads the conjugate beam with the M/EI diagram of the real beam (bending moment diagram divided by flexural rigidity EI).

q: 7. Bending moment at A of the following beam is equal to (refer to image 1666)
explain: At a simple end support or hinge, the internal bending moment is zero.

q: 8. The slope and the deflection at a section in a loaded beam cannot be found out by :
explain: Rankine's method is typically used for earth pressure or column buckling, not for determining beam deflection.

q: 9. For the beam shown in figure, the shear force at A is equal to (refer to image 1667):
explain: For a beam with a triangular load (zero at A, peak at B), the total load is $wl/2$ and the reaction at the lighter end A is $wl/6$.

q: 10. Prestressing to a large extent removes the disadvantages which a conventional reinforced concrete structure suffers as compared to a comparable :
explain: Prestressing allows concrete to span longer distances and remain crack-free, making it competitive with steel structures.

q: 11. For a cantilever with a uniformly distributed load of total W over entire length L, the max bending moment is :
explain: If W is the total load ($w \cdot L$), the moment at the fixed end is $W \cdot (L/2) = WL/2$.

q: 12. The load, required to produce a unit deflection in a spring is called :
explain: Stiffness ($k$) is defined as Force per unit displacement ($F/\delta$).

q: 13. In approximate analysis of building frames under lateral loads, the point of contraflexure in columns is assumed at
explain: Methods like the Portal and Cantilever methods assume the point of zero moment (contraflexure) is at the mid-height of the column.

q: 14. A plane structure is a structure
options: the various members of which lie in a plane
the thickness of various members of which will be very small
in which there will not be any bending moment
explain: A plane (2D) structure is one where all members and loads lie within a single plane.

q: 15. A dam is a
explain: A dam has all three dimensions (length, height, and thickness/width) of comparable significant magnitude, making it a three-dimensional structure.

q: 16. A beam is a
explain: A beam's length is much larger than its cross-sectional dimensions, classifying it as a one-dimensional structure.

q: 17. A slab is a
explain: A slab has length and width much larger than its thickness, classifying it as a two-dimensional structure.

q: 18. A plane structure when subjected to a force lying outside the plane will be
explain: A plane structure is designed to resist in-plane forces; a force acting out of its plane (out-of-plane) causes instability since it cannot properly resist such loading.

q: 19. The bending moment diagram for a simply supported beam loaded in its centre is
explain: For a simply supported beam with a central point load, the BMD is a symmetric (isosceles) triangle peaking at midspan.

q: 20. The bending moment at a section tends to bend or deflect the beam and the internal stresses resist bending. The resistance offered by the internal stresses, to the bending, is called
explain: The internal resisting stress developed within a beam's cross-section to counter the external bending moment is termed bending stress.

q: 21. When a cantilever beam is loaded at its free end, the maximum compressive stress will develop at
explain: For a cantilever loaded downward at its free end, the top fibres near the fixed support stretch (tension) while the bottom fibres compress, so maximum compressive stress develops at the bottom fibre.

q: 22. In a beam subjected to pure bending, the intensity of stress in any fibre is ............. the distance of the fibre from the neutral axis.
explain: From the flexure formula σ = My/I, bending stress varies linearly (directly proportional) with distance y from the neutral axis.

q: 23. A the neutral axis of a beam, the shear stress is
explain: For most common sections (rectangular, circular), the shear stress distribution is parabolic and peaks at the neutral axis (where it is maximum), not zero.

q: 24. The maximum bending moment due to an isolated load in a three hinged parabolic arch (span l, rise h) having one of its hinges at the crown, occurs on either side of the crown at a distance
explain: For a three-hinged parabolic arch with crown hinge, standard analysis shows the maximum bending moment due to an isolated load occurs at a distance l/(2√3) from the crown.

q: 25. A concentrated load P is supported by the free end of a quadrantal ring AB whose end B is fixed. The ratio of the vertical to horizontal deflections of the end A is
explain: For a quadrant ring under an end load, applying Castigliano's theorem to find vertical and horizontal deflection components gives a ratio of π/2.

q: 26. The moment required to rotate the near end of a prismatic beam through a unit angle without translation, the far end being simply supported is given by
explain: The rotational stiffness of a prismatic member with the far end simply supported (pinned) is 3EI/L, a standard slope-deflection method coefficient.

q: 27. The moment required to rotate the near end of a prismatic beam through a unit angle without translation, the far end being fixed is given by
explain: The rotational stiffness of a prismatic member with the far end fixed is 4EI/L, the standard slope-deflection stiffness coefficient.

q: 28. If M is the external moment which rotates the near end of a prismatic beam without translation ( the far end being fixed), then the moment induced at the far end is
options: M/2 in same direction as M
M/2 in opposite direction as M
explain: The carry-over factor for a prismatic member with the far end fixed is 1/2, meaning half the applied moment M is carried over to the far end in the same rotational sense.

q: 29. The ordinates of influence line diagram for bending moment always has the dimensions of
explain: An influence line for bending moment plots the moment produced at a section per unit load moving across the span; since moment = force×length, per unit force this ratio has dimensions of length.

q: 30. A cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load W over its full length is propped at its free end such that it is at the level of the fixed end. The bending moment will be zero at its free end also at
explain: For a propped cantilever with UDL and prop bringing the free end to the fixed-end level, analysis shows the bending moment is zero at the free end and again at 3/4 of the length measured from the free end.

q: 31. A simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load over its whole span, is propped at the centre of the span so that the beam is held to the level of the end supports. The reaction of the prop will be
explain: For a beam propped at midspan and brought level with the end supports under UDL, standard analysis gives the prop reaction as 5/8 of the total distributed load.

q: 32. The locus of reaction of a two hinged semi circular arch is
explain: As a moving load traverses a two-hinged semicircular arch, the locus of the resultant reaction at the support traces a straight line.

q: 33. The bending moment in a cable carrying a system of loads will be
explain: A flexible cable, by its nature, can carry only axial tension and adjusts its shape (funicular shape) so that bending moment is zero everywhere along its length.

q: 34. The ILD for horizontal thrust at the support of a three hinged arch when a concentrated load passes over the span is
options: a triangle with maximum ordinate at the center
a triangle with maximum ordinate at one of the supports
a parabola with maximum ordinate at the center
explain: As a unit load moves across a three-hinged arch, the influence line for horizontal thrust is a triangle peaking at the crown (mid-span), i.e., maximum ordinate at the center.

q: 35. A multi span continuous beam is simply supported at the two ends. One of the intermediate supports sinks with respect to other supports. Due to this settlement, the bending moment will get modified at
options: only the two supports adjacent to the one that sinks
all the supports except the two end supports
explain: Support settlement in a continuous beam affects the bending moments at all intermediate supports (due to the continuity/redundancy), but the two simply supported end supports (already zero moment) remain unaffected.

q: 36. In column analogy method, the area of an analogous column for a fixed beam of span L and flexural rigidity EI is taken as
explain: In the column analogy method, the analogous column's cross-sectional area is taken as L/EI, corresponding to the M/EI diagram base.

q: 37. In slope deflection equations, the deformations are considered to be caused by
options: both shear force and bending moment
explain: The slope-deflection method idealizes members as being deformed (bent) due to bending moment only, neglecting shear and axial deformations.

q: 38. Principle of superposition is applicable when
options: deflections are linear functions of applied forces
the action of applied forces will be affected by small deformations of the structure
explain: The principle of superposition holds when the structural response (deflections, forces) is a linear function of the applied loads — the fundamental condition for combining effects of multiple loads.

q: 39. The arches meant for supporting uniformly distributed loads, to avoid any bending moment must be
explain: For an arch to carry a uniformly distributed load (per unit horizontal length) with zero bending moment throughout, its shape must be parabolic, matching the funicular shape for such loading.

q: 40. An arch can be treated as curved beam .............
options: whose ends are restrained against horizontal movement
whose ends do not provide any reaction
explain: An arch functions structurally as a curved beam whose supports restrain horizontal movement, allowing the horizontal thrust to develop and enabling the arch action.

q: 41. The line of thrust of the linear arch is
options: the imaginary link work of thrust for a given set of loads
explain: The line of thrust represents the locus of resultant force (like an imaginary funicular/linkwork polygon) for a given set of loads on the arch.

q: 42. The moment in the arch will be zero if .............
options: the arch axis coincides with the line of thrust
the arch axis is parallel to the line of thrust
explain: Bending moment at any arch section equals the horizontal thrust times the perpendicular offset between the arch axis and the line of thrust; this moment vanishes only when the arch axis exactly coincides with the thrust line.

q: 43. The eddy theorem is valid for
explain: Eddy's theorem, which relates the bending moment in an arch to the vertical intercept between the arch and the linear arch (thrust line), is derived specifically for vertical loads.

q: 44. If he shear force long a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is
explain: Since dM/dx = Shear Force, a zero shear force at a section indicates the bending moment is at a local extreme (maximum or minimum) at that point.

q: 45. A cantilever beam rectangular in cross-section is subjected to an isolated load at its free end. If the width of the beam is doubled, the deflection of the free end will be changed in the ratio of
explain: Since deflection δ ∝ 1/I and I ∝ b (width) for a rectangular section, doubling the width halves the deflection.

q: 46. The ratio of the maximum deflections of a simply supported beam with a central load W and of a cantilever of same length and with a load W at its free end is
explain: Comparing WL³/48EI (simply supported, central load) to WL³/3EI (cantilever, end load) gives a ratio of (1/48)/(1/3) = 1/16.

q: 47. In the simultaneous equations derived from slope deflection method, the matrix formed by the coefficients of various rotations will have
options: all elements along the diagonal zero
diagonal symmetry with diagonal element predominant in that respective equation
explain: The stiffness matrix from slope-deflection equations is symmetric, with diagonal (self-stiffness) terms typically dominant compared to off-diagonal (coupling) terms.

q: 48. The maximum bending moment due to a train of wheel loads on a simply supported girder .............
options: always occurs at the center of span
always occurs under a wheel load
never occurs under a wheel load
explain: For moving wheel loads on a simply supported girder, the absolute maximum bending moment always occurs directly under one of the wheel loads (specifically under the load nearest the resultant of the load system), not necessarily at midspan.

q: 49. The fixed support in a real beam becomes in the conjugate beam a
explain: In the conjugate beam method, a fixed support (zero slope, zero deflection) in the real beam transforms into a free end in the conjugate beam.

q: 50. When a single load W moves over a simply supported beam, the maximum bending moment at a section will occur when the load is placed
explain: For a single moving load, the bending moment at a given section is maximum precisely when that load is positioned directly over the section itself.
